_doc: Keystone v3.1 Dimension 14 — Accessibility. First audit. Run per TEMPLATE, not per page: 180 pages off these templates share one verdict, and a finding on a template blocks that template's first publish as a P0.
rule_source: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines, referenced not copied (Keystone 16.5) — fetched fresh at run time.
headline: The audit's biggest finding was not a defect in the markup — it was that the design layer did not exist. With no stylesheet, five of Dimension 14's criteria (focus state, contrast, tap target, reduced motion, skip-link visibility) were unimplemented rather than failing, which is a worse position and an invisible one.

findings_and_fixes.finding: The services submenu was a bare nested <ul> with no disclosure control. With no JavaScript in this build that resolves to either a CSS :hover dropdown — unreachable by keyboard, unusable on touch — or a permanently open list.
findings_and_fixes.rule: Every interactive element reachable and actuable by keyboard in a sensible order.
findings_and_fixes.fix: Rebuilt on <details>/<summary>. That is a real disclosure widget: focusable, operable with Enter and Space, exposes its expanded state to assistive technology, and needs no script. On a zero-JS static build it is the correct construction rather than a fallback. The services hub also stays a direct link inside the menu, so the disclosure is never the only path in.

findings_and_fixes.finding: No stylesheet existed. Focus states, WCAG AA contrast, 44px tap targets, prefers-reduced-motion and skip-link visibility were therefore all unimplemented.
findings_and_fixes.fix: Wrote src/styles/base.css as one file carrying both the Keystone 1.3 named brand palette and the accessibility floor — deliberately together, because a colour is not chosen and then checked for contrast, it is chosen because it clears contrast against the ground it sits on. Contrast ratios are recorded inline per token. Includes :focus-visible with a two-layer ring drawn against the page ground so it survives on both themes, 44px minimum tap targets with touch-action: manipulation, a reduced-motion block, and a skip link that becomes visible on focus.

findings_and_fixes.finding: The brand link wrapped a logo image whose alt text was the business name, so the link's accessible name was the business name rather than its destination. The header call link's only text was a string of digits, which reads as digits to anyone moving by links.
findings_and_fixes.fix: Logo alt emptied and the link given aria-label "<name> — home"; the call link given aria-label "Call <name> on <number>" with the visible digits marked aria-hidden.

findings_and_fixes.finding: aria-labelledby pointed at a hardcoded id. A duplicate id on a page breaks the association silently for every assistive technology reading it. The contract is one FAQ block per URL — but a contract is not an enforcement mechanism.
findings_and_fixes.fix: The id is now a prop, so a second block on a page is addressable rather than broken.

findings_and_fixes.finding:
In the spoke-and-wheel block, two link lists were introduced by

labels. A screen reader moving by structure heard two anonymous lists.
findings_and_fixes.fix: Labels promoted to <h3>. Same visual weight, and they become navigable landmarks.

findings_and_fixes.finding: Guarantee link text read "See the terms", which is not descriptive out of context.

instrument.script: scripts/a11y.mjs, wired into npm run verify
instrument.gates: Findings fail the build. This is the one gate v3.2 ADDED rather than retired, and it does not carry the shipping-blocker problem the retired gates had: it is fixed once, in one file, and then it is fixed for every page off that template.
instrument.a_bug_it_caught_in_itself: The first run produced a false positive — a nav containing two SIBLING lists was flagged as a nested hover menu, because the check matched any two <ul> tags rather than actual nesting. Fixed with depth counting. A noisy check is how a harness gets ignored, so this mattered more than the finding would have.

what_this_does_not_cover: Focus ORDER — static analysis cannot judge whether the tab sequence makes sense.
Rendered contrast against a real background stack, as opposed to the token ratios recorded in the stylesheet.
Whether a page makes sense to someone actually using it with a screen reader.
Zoom to 200% and 320px width behaviour, which needs a browser.
Any template not yet written — the problem, library, compliance, case-study and blog routes do not exist, and each will need its own pass before its first publish.
dimension_14_status: UNSCORED. Six findings raised and six fixed, but Part 10 says to score from measurement and the items above under what_this_does_not_cover have not been measured. A score before a browser pass would be exactly the kind of flattering number the standard warns against.
